clue.text: Famous singer put registration number back on car

parts.note: a Jag is the informal name for a Jaguar car

indicators.note: back means the short form for registration is turned round before being put on the car

parts.note: REG is the short form of registration, as on a vehicle's number plate

explanation.surface: A celebrity has their personalised number plate refitted to their vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REG into GER, which is put on (after) JAG. Mick Jagger fronts the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rolling Stones' frontman is one of rock's most celebrated vocalists.

clue.text: Merry chap eating lettuce

indicators.note: eating means the word for chap takes the lettuce inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: Joe is a generic name for an ordinary man or chap
cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine

explanation.surface: A cheerful man is munching on a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and humorous, a jokey kind of cheerfulness.

clue.text: Speak and read French dialect

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly or chatter
to con is an old word for studying or reading something closely

explanation.surface: Someone is told to talk and read in a regional French tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascon is the Occitan variety spoken in Gascony, in south-west France.

clue.text: Athlete finally joins opening race

indicators.note: finally picks out only the last letter of the word athlete

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A runner finally joins in at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a sporting contest, one item on the programme of a meeting.

clue.text: Non-striker promises to settle in plant

parts.note: a scab is a worker who refuses to join a strike
IOUs are written promises to settle a debt

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker promises to put down roots at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests the factory where the strike is happening; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a flowering meadow plant with pincushion-like blooms.

clue.text: Large vessel coming from ports in E China

indicators.note: coming from suggests the answer is produced out of these letters once reshuffled

explanation.surface: A huge ship sails out of harbours in eastern China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E China' reads as eastern China, but E is just one more letter in the anagram pool.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large cargo vessel carrying goods in standard steel boxes.

clue.text: Humour: something missing in Bible originally

indicators.note: in places the word for something missing inside the rearranged name of the book
originally hints that the holy book's letters stood in some earlier order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a lack is something missing, an absence

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that comedy is absent from the original Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges BIBLE as BBILE, and 'in' puts LACK inside it. 'Humour' is the medieval bodily fluid, not comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Black bile was one of the four bodily humours of medieval medicine, linked with melancholy.

clue.text: I'll measure distance travelled round stately building over brief period

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
dome is a poetic word for a stately building, as in Coleridge's stately pleasure-dome

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for period is dropped

parts.note: a term is a period, such as a school term

explanation.surface: A guide will measure the walk round a mansion over a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the last letter from TERM. The clue speaks as the instrument itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is the instrument in a vehicle that records the miles covered.

clue.text: It has firm quality: cover it in sauce

indicators.note: in places the cover and it inside the word for the sauce

parts.note: soy is a salty sauce made from fermented soya beans
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A dish is said to firm up nicely once smothered in sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidity is the state of being hard and compact, a firm quality.

clue.text: Belgian lager popularly available in can, governor

indicators.note: in places the name of the lager inside the word can

parts.note: Stella is the everyday name for Stella Artois, a Belgian lager

explanation.surface: A popular Belgian beer is sold in tins, reports an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan was the governor or keeper of a castle.

clue.text: Will he aim to hurtle round bend at high speed?

definitions.text: Will he aim to hurtle round bend at high speed?

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the letter for bend
to hurtle suggests the letters fly about wildly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: S is a bend shaped like the letter, as in an S-bend
a ton is slang for a hundred miles an hour, a high speed

explanation.surface: Will this driver try to race through a corner at top speed?
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue describes the racing driver. 'to hurtle' rearranges WILL HE AIM as LEWIHAMIL and 'round' puts S inside; TON is British slang for 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Formula One champion is famous for taking corners at great speed.

clue.text: What a traveller might have to pay in group of islands

definitions.text: What a traveller might have to pay
definitions.meaning: split as an article plus a word for a fee charged for using a road or bridge
a ring of coral islets enclosing a lagoon

explanation.surface: What a tourist might pay to visit an island chain.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition needs the answer split after its first letter, into an article and a road charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it is a road-use charge; whole, it is a ring-shaped coral reef of islets round a lagoon.

clue.text: Wear polo?

definitions.meaning: polo is an example of a game, the question mark flagging the example

explanation.surface: Is this garment a polo shirt?
explanation.definitionFit: To show off a hat is to wear it proudly, and polo is a game played on horseback.

clue.text: Lack of time said to make you trembly

indicators.note: said means the two words are spoken and heard as a different phrase

parts.note: lack is need and a time is a week, so a week's need, written week then need

explanation.surface: Being short of time leaves a person shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with wobbly legs from fear is shaky and faint-hearted.

clue.text: Feeling of foreboding here — soldiers overwhelmed by it

parts.note: to be present is to be here

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the soldiers are engulfed inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
men is a common word for soldiers or troops

explanation.surface: Someone senses doom as troops are swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuitive sense that something, usually bad, is about to happen.

clue.text: Bully without a form of support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the bullying word goes around the a

parts.note: to bluster is to bully with loud empty threats

explanation.surface: A thug lacks any kind of support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but is the old 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short posts holding up a handrail.

clue.text: In 5 perhaps spots British safety feature

indicators.note: In places the spots and British inside the word for the vessel at 5

parts.note: the large vessel at 5 Down is one example of a carrier
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: On a big cargo vessel, perhaps, British spots mark safety equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside guardrail stops vehicles veering off the carriageway, protecting drivers.

clue.text: Nuts over time responsible for harm

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word for nuts is turned upside down

parts.note: nuts means mad, crazy
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Crazy behaviour over the years caused harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean injury or impairment inflicted on something.

clue.text: Dog given fish and meat at regular intervals

parts.note: a bass is a fish

indicators.note: at regular intervals takes every other letter of meat

explanation.surface: A dog is fed fish and meat at set times.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound bred for tracking by scent.

clue.text: Fastidious squire drives out Irish sect

indicators.note: drives out means the letters for Irish are expelled from the word squire

parts.note: the Amish are a strict Christian sect

explanation.surface: A fussy landowner evicts a group of Irish worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily disgusted or overly scrupulous people are fussy about what they touch.

clue.text: Drama near a beach in Spain

parts.note: a play is a drama for the stage

explanation.surface: A theatre production is staged close to a Spanish beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Playa is the Spanish word for a beach, familiar from resort names.

clue.text: Group of law enforcers repossessing houses

indicators.note: houses means the word repossessing holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Bailiffs are seizing people's homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band summoned by a sheriff to help keep order.

clue.text: Explorer in middle part of boat ready to return

indicators.note: middle part of takes the letters of boat without its first and last
to return means the word for ready is read backwards

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: An adventurer sits in the centre of a boat, prepared to go home.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Antarctic polar party member who walked out into the blizzard on Scott's 1912 expedition.

clue.text: Bistros serving variety of pasta, also cakes

indicators.note: variety of suggests a different arrangement of the letters of pasta

parts.note: cakes of soap or chocolate are bars

explanation.surface: Restaurants offer a range of pasta dishes and desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish snack restaurants serving small plates are casual eating places like bistros.

clue.text: Footballer first to moan on entering a players training ground

indicators.note: first to picks out only the opening letter of moan
entering means on goes inside the a and the drama school

parts.note: RADA, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, is a London school where actors train
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sportsman is first to complain on arriving at an actors' academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts ON inside ARADA (A plus RADA). 'players' are actors, not sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine star of the 1986 World Cup, famed for the Hand of God goal, played football.

clue.text: Another showing of programme about garden fertiliser

parts.note: re means about or concerning
peat is dug into gardens to enrich the soil

explanation.surface: A rerun of a gardening show about compost.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun of a TV show is a second broadcast of it.
